newsitem.title: INDIA: India to invite private offers to widen highways.
newsitem.headline: India to invite private offers to widen highways.

text.p: India will soon invite offers from private firms to widen some of its two-lane highways to four-lane highways, a senior government official said on Wednesday.

"We will now bring packages (of offer) for four-laning national highways," S. Sundar, the highest-ranking civil servant in the Surface Transport Ministry, told a seminar on ports and roads organised by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII).

He said the government intended to widen 27,000 km (16,875 miles) of highways into four-lane roads, and had set a priority to upgrade 7,000 km (4,375 miles) of these roads. Of this, 3,000 km (1,875) were expected to be built by the private sector, he said.
India opened up its roads sector to private and foreign firms for build-own-transfer (BOT) contracts under an economic reform programme launched in 1991.
Private firms would be allowed to levy toll charges on the roads they build.

A government committee has estimated that India needs 320 billion rupees ($9.0 billion) over the next five years and 630 billion rupees ($17.5 billion) over the following five years to build highways.

Progress in attracting private capital to build roads has been slow, since the process involves considerable government efforts in land acquisition and environmental approvals and financial risks linked to high capital requirments.
"Fiscal incentives for implementing projects are not adequate and need to be enhanced," Sundar said.
India has declared a five-year tax holiday and a 30 percent tax rebate on profits for another five years for investors in highway projects.

The government has also stepped up budgetary support to the National Highway Authority of India (NHAI), which is charged with overseeing private sector work in road building. The NHAI can now invest in companies building roads.
"We have not given up expressways but we have not given them priority," Sundar said.
He was referring to a proposal to build new high-speed roads linking major Indian cities.
Malaysia's Renong Berhad group had approached the Indian government with a proposal to build such roads. ($1=35.8 rupees)
